fanoutqa_035102.t: Specialized high schools in New York City :: History :: chunk_0009
fanoutqa_035102.x:
Specialized high schools in New York City :: History :: chunk_0009
In 1934, Stuyvesant implemented a system of entrance examinations. The examination was developed with the assistance of [Columbia University](/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University"), and the program was later expanded to include the newly founded Bronx Science and Brooklyn Tech.[[6]](#cite_note-blaufarb1-6)

Their status as specialized schools was frequently threatened by factions within the New York City school system and government. As a way to preserve their special status, in 1972, the Hecht-Calandra Act was passed by the [New York State Legislature](/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature"), designating these schools as specialized science and math high schools for New York City. The Act called for a uniform exam in math and science to be administered for admission to these schools, in keeping with the uniform examination that had already been required by the New York City Board of Education for admission to these schools. The School of Performing Arts and The High School of Music & Art (consolidated in 1984 into LaGuardia High School) were also designated by the legislature as specialized high schools, and admission was by audition and portfolio rather than examination, in keeping with their artistic mission.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Staten Island Tech began in 1982 as an annex of Ralph R. McKee Vocational-Technical High School and was made an independent high school in May 1988. HSAS, HSMSE, and QHSSYC were opened in 2002. Brooklyn Latin was established in 2006. All of these schools are required by state law to admit students based on the uniform Specialized High Schools Admissions Test,[[8]](#cite_note-8) and positions are assigned on a ranked system, depending on the number of seats available and how many applicants requested a given school.

The Great Smoky Mountains National Park is a major tourist attraction in the region. It has been the most visited national park for many years, with over 14.1 million recreational visitors (tourists) in 2021.[[104]](#cite_note-Visits-104)

The park has three main entrances, located in Gatlinburg, Cherokee, and Townsend.[[105]](#cite_note-105) [U.S. Route 441](/wiki/U.S._Route_441 "U.S. Route 441") (US 441, Newfound Gap Road) is the main road through the park, and runs between Cherokee and Gatlinburg.[[106]](#cite_note-parkmap-106) The Gatlinburg entrance to the park is the busiest, and is also the southern terminus of the [Great Smoky Mountains Parkway](/wiki/Great_Smoky_Mountains_Parkway "Great Smoky Mountains Parkway"), a highway which connects the park to Pigeon Forge, Sevierville, and [Interstate 40](/wiki/Interstate_40_in_Tennessee "Interstate 40 in Tennessee") to the north.[[107]](#cite_note-regionmap-107)

Roosevelt was homeschooled. Biographer [H. W. Brands](/wiki/H._W._Brands "H. W. Brands") wrote that, "The most obvious drawback...was uneven coverage of...various areas of...knowledge."[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands199749-11) He was solid in geography and bright in history, biology, French, and German; however, he struggled in mathematics and the classical languages.

In September 1876, he entered [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"). His father instructed him to, "take care of your morals first, your health next, and finally your studies."[[11]](#cite_note-12) His father's sudden death in 1878 devastated Roosevelt.[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMiller199280–82-13) He inherited US$60,000 (equivalent to $1.71 million in 2024), on which he could live comfortably for the rest of his life.[[13]](#cite_note-NYT14-14)

His father, a devout [Presbyterian](/wiki/Presbyterianism "Presbyterianism"), had regularly led the family in prayers. While at Harvard, young adult Theodore emulated him by teaching Sunday School for more than three years at the Episcopal [Christ Church](/wiki/Christ_Church_(Cambridge,_Massachusetts) "Christ Church (Cambridge, Massachusetts)") in [Cambridge, Massachusetts](/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts"). When the minister at Christ Church insisted he become an Episcopalian to continue teaching, Roosevelt declined, and began teaching a mission class in a poor section of Cambridge.[[14]](#cite_note-15)

Roosevelt did well in science, philosophy, and rhetoric courses, but struggled in Latin and Greek. He was already an accomplished naturalist and a published [ornithologist](/wiki/Ornithology "Ornithology"), and studied biology intently. Since 2008, Messi has been in a relationship with [Antonela Roccuzzo](/wiki/Antonela_Roccuzzo "Antonela Roccuzzo"), who he eventually married on 30 June 2017 in their hometown of [Rosario](/wiki/Rosario,_Santa_Fe "Rosario, Santa Fe").[[394]](#cite_note-425)[[395]](#cite_note-426) Roccuzzo is the cousin of Messi's childhood best friend, [Lucas Scaglia](/wiki/Lucas_Scaglia "Lucas Scaglia"), and Messi has known her since he was five years old.[[396]](#cite_note-427) After keeping their relationship private for a year, Messi first confirmed their romance in an interview in January 2009, before going public a month later during a carnival in [Sitges](/wiki/Sitges "Sitges") after the [Barcelona–Espanyol derby](/wiki/Derbi_Barcelon%C3%AD "Derbi Barceloní").[[397]](#cite_note-428)

Messi and Roccuzzo have three sons. To celebrate Roccuzzo's first pregnancy, Messi placed the ball under his shirt after scoring in Argentina's 4–0 win against Ecuador on 2 June 2012, before confirming the pregnancy in an interview two weeks later.[[398]](#cite_note-429) The child, a son named Thiago, was born in Barcelona on 2 November 2012.[[399]](#cite_note-430) In April 2015, Messi confirmed that they were expecting another child.[[400]](#cite_note-431) In October 2017, his wife announced they were expecting their third child.[[401]](#cite_note-432) Messi and his family are [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic "Catholic").[[402]](#cite_note-433)

Messi enjoys a close relationship with his immediate family members, particularly his mother, Celia, whose face he has tattooed on his left shoulder. His professional affairs are largely run as a family business: his father, Jorge, has been his agent since he was 14, and his oldest brother, Rodrigo, handles his daily schedule and publicity. [Astoria](/wiki/Astoria,_Oregon "Astoria, Oregon"), at the mouth of the Columbia River, was the first permanent English-speaking settlement west of the [Rockies](/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") in what is now the U.S. [Oregon City](/wiki/Oregon_City,_Oregon "Oregon City, Oregon"), at the end of the Oregon Trail, was the Oregon Territory's first incorporated city, and was its first capital from 1848 until 1852, when the capital was moved to Salem. [Bend](/wiki/Bend,_Oregon "Bend, Oregon"), near the geographic center of the state, is one of the ten fastest-growing metropolitan areas in the U.S.[[97]](#cite_note-99) In southern Oregon, [Medford](/wiki/Medford,_Oregon "Medford, Oregon") is a rapidly growing metro area and is home to the [Rogue Valley International–Medford Airport](/wiki/Rogue_Valley_International%E2%80%93Medford_Airport "Rogue Valley International–Medford Airport"), the state's third-busiest airport. The [Alpine Rhine](/wiki/Alpine_Rhine "Alpine Rhine") border between Liechtenstein and Switzerland (view towards the [Swiss Alps](/wiki/Swiss_Alps "Swiss Alps"))

Liechtenstein is situated in the Upper [Rhine](/wiki/Rhine "Rhine") valley of the European [Alps](/wiki/Alps "Alps") and is bordered to the east by the Austrian state of [Vorarlberg](/wiki/Vorarlberg "Vorarlberg"), to the south by the [canton of Grisons](/wiki/Canton_of_Grisons "Canton of Grisons") (Switzerland) and to the west by the [canton of St. Gallen](/wiki/Canton_of_St._Gallen "Canton of St. Gallen") (Switzerland). The Rhine forms the entire western border of Liechtenstein. Measured south to north the country is about 24 km (15 mi) long. In 1943, an [inland canal](/wiki/Liechtenstein_inland_canal "Liechtenstein inland canal") was built in the country connecting to the Rhine.[[51]](#cite_note-51)

Its highest point, [Grauspitz](/wiki/Grauspitz "Grauspitz"), is 2,599 m (8,527 ft). Despite its Alpine location, prevailing southerly winds make the climate comparatively mild. In winter, the mountain slopes are well suited to winter sports. New [surveys](/wiki/Surveying "Surveying") using more accurate measurements of the country's borders in 2006 have set its area at 160 km2 (62 sq mi), with borders of 77.9 km (48.4 mi).[[52]](#cite_note-52) Liechtenstein's borders are 1.9 km (1.2 mi) longer than previously thought.[[53]](#cite_note-5

**Marit Bjørgen** (born 21 March 1980) is a former Norwegian [cross-country skier](/wiki/Cross-country_skiing_(sport) "Cross-country skiing (sport)"). She is ranked first in the all-time Cross-Country World Cup rankings with 114 individual victories. Bjørgen is also the most successful sprinter in [Cross-Country World Cup](/wiki/FIS_Cross-Country_World_Cup "FIS Cross-Country World Cup") history, with 29 victories. She [headed the medal table](/wiki/List_of_2010_Winter_Olympics_medal_winners#Medal_leaders "List of 2010 Winter Olympics medal winners") at the 2010 Winter Olympics by winning five medals, including three gold. A five-time Olympian, her five Olympic medals at the [2018 Pyeongchang](/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") Games brought her total number of medals up to a record 15, making her the [most decorated Winter Olympian](/wiki/List_of_multiple_Winter_Olympic_medallists "List of multiple Winter Olympic medallists") of all time and the [third-most decorated Olympian](/wiki/List_of_multiple_Olympic_medalists "List of multiple Olympic medalists") of all time.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

On 6 April 2018, Bjørgen announced her retirement from cross-country skiing following the [2017–18 season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_FIS_Cross-Country_World_Cup "2017–18 FIS Cross-Country World Cup").[[3]](#cite_note-3) In May 2020, she announced that she would return to competition with long-distance cross-country ski squad Team Ragde Eiendom, with a focus on competing in [Vasaloppet](/wiki/Vasaloppet "Vasaloppet") in March 2021.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

On 28 April 2022, she announced the end of her career by also finishing her long-distance career.[[5]](#cite_note-5)
